review.summary: Round 9 reviews the whole TASK-069A branch at the round-8 fix commit. All five round-8 findings are verified fixed: the narrowed allowlist claim, the step-decides-status wording with the lock-error selection in ADR-015 and TASK-069I, TASK-069F tests for the throttled token-time client update, the stated punctuation trade-off, and rewrapped lines. A word-level diff and a rendered HTML comparison confirm the rewrap changed no words or rendering. Scope is still documentation-only. likec4@1.60.0 validate passes and the committed PNGs are byte-identical to a fresh export with the README command; relative links and anchors resolve; the review records validate. Five new findings, four low and one info, all wording or test placement: an accidental numbered list in ADR-015, leftover classification wording in AI.md and the concept, an over-broad 503 sentence, an overstatement of what the redirect host proves for loopback clients, and the placement of TASK-069F's PostgreSQL case.

findings.summary: A wrapped line in ADR-015 starts with a number and a period, so Markdown renders a numbered list in the middle of a sentence.
findings.rationale: The lock timeout bullet wraps before the step number, and CommonMark lets an ordered list starting at one interrupt a paragraph, cutting the sentence in two. This came in with the round-7 fix.
findings.recommendation: Rewrap so no continuation line starts with a number followed by a period.

findings.summary: AI.md and the concept still say apply errors are classified by step, not by error type.
findings.rationale: That is the claim the previous round narrowed in ADR-015 and TASK-069I: the step alone decides the status, but the retryable response in the first steps depends on recognising the lock error.
findings.recommendation: Use ADR-015's wording in both files.

findings.summary: ADR-015 says any other error in the first steps is 503, although those steps also produce the not-submitted 409 and review_stale.
findings.rationale: Read literally, the new bullet contradicts the bullets around it, and the same rule is now stated several times in that section.
findings.recommendation: Say any other unexpected error, and optionally merge the duplicated bullets.

findings.summary: ADR-015 overstates what showing the redirect host verifies, especially for loopback redirect URIs.
findings.rationale: The consent page only displays the host; the server checks it against the allowlist. For loopback redirect URIs the host identifies no client, so any local program can register with a known client's name and look identical on the consent page, and this limitation is not stated.
findings.recommendation: Say the server verifies the host against the allowlist, and state that for loopback URIs the host only shows the code goes to a program on the user's own machine, so local clients cannot be told apart by name or host.

findings.summary: TASK-069F's PostgreSQL wait case is listed only under testing, lacks its run command, and overlaps with TASK-069E's lock test.
findings.rationale: The module exists from TASK-069E, so the placement is coherent, but TASK-069F does not make the case an acceptance criterion or include the database-URL command and CI note, and TASK-069E still mentions the token-time wait that only TASK-069F can test.
findings.recommendation: Add the case to TASK-069F's acceptance criteria with the command and CI note, and limit TASK-069E's lock test to authorize against cleanup and a raw grant insert.

prior_finding_dispositions.rationale: ADR-015 now limits the allowlist claim to look-alike letters from other scripts and states that a client can still copy a known client's name, which is why the name is labelled self-declared; a leftover overclaim about the redirect host is recorded as a new finding.

ADR-015 and TASK-069I now say the step alone decides whether the status changes and that the lock-not-available error in the lock step selects apply_in_progress, with TASK-069K and M consistent; leftovers in AI.md and the concept are recorded as a new finding.

TASK-069F now tests that code exchange and refresh update the client's last-used time and that a second issuance within five minutes does not, and adds a PostgreSQL wait case; placement details are recorded as a new finding.
ADR-015 and TASK-069O now state that ASCII punctuation outside the set is also rejected, with examples of rejected names; the allowlist itself is unchanged, as the optional widening was not taken.
The affected lines are rewrapped; a word-level diff and rendered HTML comparison show no changed words or rendering apart from intended content edits.
